column1: # known-local-red.tsv — the LOCAL known-red set, as DATA (your-org/nexus-code#1445).
# A full local suite run on an operator's live board is not green on pristine
# `dev`, and the standing rule is "iterate locally, the PR is the last step".
# An unqualified "the local suite must be green" is therefore unsatisfiable,
# and a bare `N failed` is a count a worker must interpret — which is a count a
# worker WILL misinterpret, in both directions: dismiss a real red as "one of
# the usual", or chase an inherited one into someone else's code.
# So the set is written down where the runner can read it. At the foot of a
# run, `watcher/run-tests.sh` partitions the FAILING SET against these rows and
# prints, beside the count, which failures are in this set and which are
# UNEXPLAINED. The local gate is `failing set ⊆ known-local-red set`; a member
# outside it blocks the push. DIFF THE SETS, NEVER THE COUNTS — equal totals
# can share zero members (#1150).
# THIS IS NOT AN ALLOWLIST FOR CI. The runner still exits 1 on any failure; a
# row here changes what is PRINTED, never the verdict. CI never reads this
# file's classes (it has no live tmux server and no board load), and a suite
# listed here still reds on a runner if it is genuinely broken.
# Columns (tab-separated): suite<TAB>class<TAB>issue<TAB>reason
#   suite   `<dir>/<file>` as the runner tags it: `watcher/test-x.sh` or
#           `monitor/test-x.sh` (basename of the parent dir + basename).
#   class   load       — passes in isolation; reds under board load
#           live-tmux  — asserts against a clean tmux server; a live board has one
#           host       — a property of this host's configuration, not of the tree
#   issue   the tracker that expires the row (`#N`); a row with no live issue
#           is a dismissal, and `test-known-local-red.sh` refuses it.
#   reason  one line, human-readable, the mechanism not the symptom.
# A row is a MEASUREMENT with a date, not a permanent exemption: re-derive it
# when the issue it names closes. Enforced by monitor/watcher/test-known-local-red.sh
# (every row names an existing suite, a valid class and an issue; the runner's
# classification is driven against a planted manifest).
